How we choose safe and trusted casinos
A big bonus is easy to advertise. A casino that pays you properly is harder to find. These are the things we check before a site makes our Canadian list:
- A licence you can verify. We look for the licence number and regulator on the site itself (for example iGaming Ontario, the Kahnawake Gaming Commission or the Malta Gaming Authority) and check it against the regulator’s register.
- Real payout times. We look at how long withdrawals actually take after verification, not what the banner promises.
- Canadian banking. CAD accounts, Interac, and at least one e-wallet option, with fees and limits shown clearly.
- Bonus terms in plain sight. Wagering, maximum bet, game weighting and expiry dates should be easy to find. Wagering far above 35x is a warning sign.
- Support that answers. Live chat that responds within a few minutes, in English and French if possible.
- Responsible gambling tools. Deposit limits, time-outs and self-exclusion you can set yourself from your account.
Is online gambling legal in Canada?
Yes, but the rules depend on your province. Canada leaves gambling to the provinces, so there isn’t one national answer.
- Ontario has a regulated, open market. Private casinos must be registered with iGaming Ontario, and Ontario players should stick to those registered sites.
- Most other provinces run their own government site, such as PlayNow in British Columbia and Manitoba, Loto-Québec in Quebec and PlayAlberta in Alberta. Alberta has also passed a law to open a regulated market to private operators, so check the latest status if you live there.
- Many Canadians outside Ontario also play at offshore casinos licensed elsewhere, such as Kahnawake, Malta or Curaçao. Players are rarely prosecuted for this, but these sites aren’t regulated by your province, so choosing a reputable operator matters even more.
The minimum age is 19 in most provinces and 18 in Alberta, Manitoba and Quebec.
Online casino games you’ll find at Canadian sites
Most Canadian-facing casinos carry hundreds or thousands of games. The main groups are:
- Slots: from three-reel classics to modern video slots and Megaways. See our guide to the best online slots sites in Canada .
- Table games: blackjack, roulette, baccarat and video poker, usually in several variants with different table limits.
- Live dealer games: real dealers streamed in HD, including live blackjack, roulette, baccarat and game shows. See our pick of live dealer casinos in Canada .
- Progressive jackpots: slots whose prize grows with every bet until someone wins it, sometimes into the millions.

Welcome bonuses: what they’re really worth
Almost every casino on this page offers a welcome package, usually a deposit match plus free spins. The headline number matters less than the wagering requirement.
Here’s a simple example. You deposit C$100 and get a 100% match, so C$100 in bonus money. If the wagering is 35x the bonus, you need to place C$3,500 in bets before you can withdraw any bonus winnings. A smaller bonus with 20x wagering can be worth more than a big one with 50x.
We compare current offers side by side in our guide to Canadian casino welcome bonuses .
Deposits and withdrawals for Canadian players
- Interac e-Transfer: the most popular choice. Deposits are instant and withdrawals usually take one to three business days.
- iDebit and Instadebit: bank-linked transfers that work well when Interac isn’t offered.
- E-wallets such as MuchBetter, Skrill and Neteller: often the fastest way to get paid, sometimes within hours.
- Visa and Mastercard: fine for deposits, but many Canadian banks block gambling transactions on credit cards, and card withdrawals are slower.
- Cryptocurrency: offered by some offshore sites. It’s fast, but prices move, and it isn’t available at provincially regulated casinos.
Tip: upload your ID and proof of address as soon as you sign up. Most payout delays come from verification, not the payment method.
Playing on your phone
Every casino on our list works in a mobile browser, and several have dedicated iOS and Android apps. You’ll get the same games, the same cashier and the same bonuses. The main difference is how easy the site is to navigate on a small screen, which is why LeoVegas ranks highly for mobile.
Play responsibly
Casino games are entertainment, not a way to make money. Set a budget before you play, use the deposit limits and time-outs in your account, and never chase losses. If gambling stops being fun, help is free and confidential. Ontario residents can call ConnexOntario at 1-866-531-2600, and players anywhere in Canada can find support through the Responsible Gambling Council (responsiblegambling.org) or their provincial GameSense program.
